There was this essay I threw together the night before, and you wrote a note at the bottom that said something like, this is the most honest thing you've written. Keep going. And I kept that paper in a shoebox all through college and through two moves across country. I ended up becoming a reporter. And now I edit a little paper in the town where I live. And every time some young writer comes into my office, all nervous and apologizing for the draft, I think about that note, and I try to do for them what you did for me. I don't think teachers hear enough about how things turn out. So I just wanted you to know. Thank you for paying attention to a kid who really wasn't making it easy. I hope you're doing well and enjoying retirement. With real gratitude, Daniel.
